entry.title: Day 65: Debugging Life While Building Dreams
entry.summary: Another day in the trenches of building something from scratch. Today felt like one of those debug sessions where you're not sure if the issue is in your code or in your brain. Hit the gym after a 2-day hiatus. There's something brutal about discipline – it doesn't just demand your time, it wants your soul. And here's the kicker: people will judge you for trying to improve but stay completely silent when you're stuck in mediocrity. Solution? Headphones on, world off. Been dealing with this weird dizziness that makes work feel like repeatedly hitting my head against a wall. Sleep's been decent, so it's not the usual suspect. Sometimes your body throws exceptions that your mind can't catch. Finally retrieved my laptop from the service center today. Felt like getting back a vital organ. Immediately dove into strategizing promotion for rthw tech, which is currently in its building phase. A friend called me a product manager today, and honestly, it felt accurate. Had an unplanned 40-minute system restart (aka desk nap) – not romanticizing it, just acknowledging that sometimes your hardware demands downtime. Made oats for dinner because the mess food continues to fail basic quality tests. Looking at the time now, tomorrow's going to run on 4 hours of sleep, but that's the price of shipping ideas. About to start part 1 of project mutiny. Which brings me to this: how many of you would be interested in trying mutiny when it's ready? It'll be free for everyone. Some days feel like debugging life in real-time while simultaneously building the future. The chaos is where the magic happens. Time to code through the night.

If you’ve ever waited impatiently for pip install to finish, or juggled multiple tools just to set up a clean Python environment—this one’s for you. In our latest post, we explore uv, a new all-in-one Python toolchain that replaces pip, venv, Python version managers, and more. MCP Elicitation provides a standardized way for servers to request additional input from users through the client during a session. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard developed by Anthropic that enables LLMs to receive data from any backend or application in a single, standardized format.
